profile.summary: ProstT5 is a protein language model that translates between a protein's amino acid sequence and a one-letter-per-residue description of its 3D structure (Foldseek 3Di tokens). Given a sequence it can predict 3Di tokens ('folding'), given 3Di tokens it can propose sequences ('inverse folding'), and its encoder gives per-residue and per-protein embeddings of either. The authors use the predicted 3Di strings for fast structure-based search with Foldseek without computing 3D structures.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: introduction; model card: Model Description, Uses

summary_quotes.text: (Protein structure-sequence T5) is a protein language model (pLM) which can translate between protein sequence and structure.
Protein structure is converted from 3D to 1D using the 3Di-tokens introduced by [Foldseek](https://github.com/steineggerlab/foldseek).

3. "Folding": Translation from sequence (AAs) to structure (3Di). The resulting 3Di strings can be used together with [Foldseek](https://github.com/steineggerlab/foldseek) for remote homology detection while avoiding to compute 3D structures explicitly.
4. "Inverse Folding": Translation from structure (3Di) to sequence (AA).
ProstT5 can now also embed 3D structures represented by 3Di tokens

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ProstT5 is a T5 encoder-decoder initialised from ProtT5-XL-U50, a model trained with span corruption on protein sequences. Structures are written as Foldseek 3Di strings, which assign each residue one of twenty structural states. Training had two steps. First the model continued the span-denoising objective on both amino acid and 3Di sequences, to learn the new tokens without forgetting amino acids. Then it was trained to translate in both directions. A prefix token sets the direction: <AA2fold> for sequence to 3Di and <fold2AA> for 3Di to sequence. 3Di letters are written in lower case so they do not clash with amino acid letters.
sections.source_locator: model card: Model Description; paper: Figure 1 caption

quotes.text: ProstT5 is a T5-based encoder-decoder model initialized with weights of the ProtT5 model
transferred protein 3D coordinates into 3Di tokens, i.e. 1D descriptions of 3D structure that assign each residue in a protein into one of twenty states
In a first step, ProstT5 learnt to represent the newly introduced 3Di-tokens by continuing the original span-denoising objective applied on 3Di- and amino acid- (AA) sequences.
Only in a second step, ProstT5 was trained on translating between the two modalities.
To avoid clashes with AA tokens, 3Di-tokens were cast to lower-case (alphabets are identical otherwise).

sections.title: Training data
sections.body: The training set was built from AlphaFoldDB predictions: clusters were expanded with diverse members, then low-confidence predictions (pLDDT below 70), proteins shorter than 30 residues and highly repetitive 3Di strings were removed. The final set has 17M proteins, which gives 34M training samples because each protein is used in both translation directions. Training first truncated sequences to 256 residues and later extended to 512.

quotes.text: The final training set contained 17M proteins (4.3M singletons with respect to the original 16M).
this corresponded to 34M training samples
we increased throughput by limiting sequence lengths to 256 (truncating longer sequences)
and increased to 512 for another 600K

The Hugging Face card's code examples contain errors; the README examples are the cleaner reference. A result should name the Hugging Face revision; this page read revision d7d097d5.

strengths.text: One model covers embedding, sequence to structure-string translation and inverse folding.

quotes.text: 1. The model can be used for traditional feature extraction.
4. "Inverse Folding": Translation from structure (3Di) to sequence (AA).

strengths.text: Predicting 3Di strings avoids full structure prediction. The authors report about 43.5 s for a 1787-protein proteome on one GPU, against 48 h for a ColabFold workflow; this is the authors' measurement.

quotes.text: took 40min 6s (±4min 38s) on CPU (Macbook M1 2020) and 43.5s (±2s) on GPU (Nvidia RTX A5000), compared to the 48h structure prediction time on GPU

strengths.text: Code, weights and training data are public under MIT, and loading needs only the transformers library.

limitations.text: The encoder-decoder translation is slow: the authors report 0.6 to 2.5 s per protein, because decoding is token by token.

quotes.text: The encoder-decoder translation is comparatively slow (0.6–2.5s/protein at an average length of 135 and 406, respectively) due to the sequential nature of the decoding process

limitations.text: Half precision works only on GPU; on CPU the model must run in full precision, which the README calls much slower.

run_guide.summary: Install the Python libraries and compute residue and per-protein embeddings for one amino acid sequence and one 3Di string with ProstT5.
prerequisites: A GPU is optional; the README says CPU works in full precision but is much slower.
Internet access to download Rostlab/ProstT5 from Hugging Face.

steps.title: Compute embeddings
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
from transformers import T5Tokenizer, T5EncoderModel
import torch
import re
device = torch.device('cuda:0' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')

tokenizer = T5Tokenizer.from_pretrained('Rostlab/ProstT5', do_lower_case=False)
model = T5EncoderModel.from_pretrained("Rostlab/ProstT5").to(device)
model.float() if device.type=='cpu' else model.half()

sequence_examples = ["PRTEINO", "strct"]
sequence_examples = [" ".join(list(re.sub(r"[UZOB]", "X", sequence))) for sequence in sequence_examples]
sequence_examples = [ "<AA2fold>" + " " + s if s.isupper() else "<fold2AA>" + " " + s
                      for s in sequence_examples
                    ]

ids = tokenizer.batch_encode_plus(sequence_examples,
                                  add_special_tokens=True,
                                  padding="longest",
                                  return_tensors='pt').to(device)

with torch.no_grad():
    embedding_repr = model(
              ids.input_ids,
              attention_mask=ids.attention_mask
              )

emb_0 = embedding_repr.last_hidden_state[0,1:8] # shape (7 x 1024)
emb_1 = embedding_repr.last_hidden_state[1,1:6] # shape (5 x 1024)
emb_0_per_protein = emb_0.mean(dim=0) # shape (1024)
PY
steps.explanation: The README's embedding example, wrapped in a shell heredoc by Rewire with its comments shortened. It embeds the toy sequence PRTEINO (with <AA2fold>) and the toy 3Di string strct (with <fold2AA>) and mean-pools the first into a 1024-value vector.
